newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-BENKENSTEIN AND BRUYNS HIT CENTURIES AS AUSTRALIA TOIL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BENKENSTEIN AND BRUYNS HIT CENTURIES AS AUSTRALIA TOIL.

text.p: Dale Benkenstein and Mark Bruyns plundered centuries as Australia's bowlers toiled in the field for much of a hot opening day of their four-day match against Natal on Thursday.
Benkenstein (103) and Bruyns (105) shared a fifth-wicket stand of 155, hauling the innings around after the home side had slumped to 45 for three.
Natal were all out for 335. Australia were 23 for no wicket in reply at the close.

It was a day of mixed fortunes for Australia's attack. New ball bowler Paul Reiffel limped off during the sixth over of the morning with a recurrence of his hamstring strain while leg-spinner Shane Warne struggled for control of line and length as he returned figures of 0-89 from 20 overs.

Yet first change seamer Jason Gillespie impressed with a hostile opening spell of 2-26 -- and a final return of 4-71 -- and left-arm wrist spinner Michael Bevan posed problems for the Natal batsmen in taking 3-56.
"Bevan was a lot more difficult to play today than Shane Warne but then Warne's got the record and you definitely can't write him off," Benkenstein said.
"Bevan is certainly not a part-time bowler and I think he'll have a big say in the test series."
Australian vice-captain Ian Healy, who was impressed with Gillespie's ability to move the ball away from the right-handed batsmen, was not unduly worried by Warne's display.
"The wicket today suited Michael (Bevan) far more as he's faster through the air," said Healy.
The 21-year-old Gillespie, challenging Andrew Bichel for a place in the Australian test line-up at the Wanderers next week, now appears to have nosed in front of his fast bowling rival.
Out-of-favour test batsman Jonty Rhodes was undone by a snorter from Glen McGrath for a brisk 20 and Natal were in relative trouble at 83 for four in the 26th over.
But Bruyns, playing a solid anchor role, and an aggressive Benkenstein then took the attack to the Australian bowlers as they added 132 during the afternoon session.

Benkenstein, dropped on 39 by substitute fielder Greg Blewett off Warne at long-on, went on to strike 13 fours and four sixes in his fourth first-class century of the season. He smashed Warne for 17 in one over.
